name: GammeV
summary: A historical light-shining-through-a-wall experiment using variable conversion lengths to search for meV-scale ALPs.
detection_principle: A movable barrier changes the effective conversion lengths on both sides of the magnet, avoiding coherence blind spots of fixed baselines at some masses; regenerated light behind the wall is detected.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2007 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for axion-like particles using a variable baseline photon regeneration technique

phases.name: GammeV ALP
phases.description: Variable-baseline light shining through a wall.

phases.name: GammeV / CHASE chameleon studies
phases.description: Afterglow searches primarily target dark-energy candidates; included as related history rather than counted separately as dedicated dark-matter experiments.

results.summary: No excess regenerated photons; constraints were placed on the particle interpretation of the earlier PVLAS anomaly.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
